titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Laborer and the Queen's Question (ch. 27)
part: ch. 27 — The Laborer and the Queen's Question
about: Solomon, speaking with Makeda, sees a sweating laborer, calls him over, and asks what separates a king from such a man; both are mortal, and God gives strength as he wills. He preaches repentance, mercy and humility over pride and the Devil. The queen praises his words and asks whom she should worship, explaining that her people bow to the sun; she has heard that Israel's God sent the Ark and the tablets by Moses, and asks whether he himself comes down to them.

sentences.t: ፳፯ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ገባራዊ ።
sentences.l: 27. Concerning laborer-ness.
sentences.i: Chapter 27: Concerning the Laborer
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፳፯ is 20 + 7 = 27. በእንተ 'concerning' takes a construct. ገባራዊ is a noun of the form ገባር 'laborer, workman' + the ending -ዊ (an adjective or abstract ending), so 'the laborer' or 'laborer-matters'; I render it 'the Laborer'. The root ገብረ 'work, do' gives ገባር 'laborer' and also አገበረ 'make (someone) work', which recurs below.

sentences.t: ወእንዘ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ይትናገራ ፡ ለንግሥት ፡ ርእዮ ፡ ለ፩ ፡ ገባር ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይጸውር ፡ እብነ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ርእሱ ፡ ወሳእረ ፡ ማይ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ክሳዱ ፡ ወስንቁ ፡ ወዓሣእኒሁ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሐቌሁ ፡ ወለዕፀውኒ ፡ ደመሮን ፡ ውስተ ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወብሉያት ፡ ወሥጡጣት ፡ አልባሲሁ ፡ ወሃፉ ፡ ያንጠበጥብ ፡ እምነ ፡ ገጹ ፡ ወማየ ፡ ሳእርኒ ፡ ይውኅዝ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰኰናሁ ።
sentences.l: And-while this he-was-speaking to-the-queen, seeing [he saw] to-one laborer while he-carries a-stone upon his-head, and-a-skin(?)-of water upon his-neck, and-his-provisions and-his-sandals(?) at his-loins, and-also-the-wood he-had-gathered-them in his-hands, and-worn and-torn his-clothes, and-sweat dripping from his-face, and-the-water-of the-skin(?) also flowing to his-feet.
sentences.i: While he was saying this to the queen, he saw a laborer carrying a stone on his head and a water-skin (?) on his neck, with his food and his sandals (?) at his waist and sticks gathered in his hands. His clothes were worn and torn, sweat dripped from his face, and the water from the skin ran down onto his feet.
sentences.n: ወእንዘ 'and while' (ወ- + እንዘ, which introduces a circumstantial clause with the imperfect). ይትናገራ 'he was speaking with her' (ተናገረ 'speak, converse' + -ኣ 'her'); the speaker is Solomon, continuing from the end of the last part. ርእዮ is a gerund-like form 'seeing' (not the 3ms perfect ርእየ), so 'he saw' by the sense. ለ፩ ገባር: ለ- marks the object, ፩ 'one', ገባር 'laborer' (from ገብረ 'work'). ይጸውር 'he carries' (ጾረ). እብነ 'stone' is accusative (-ä); ዲበ 'upon'. ሳእረ ማይ: I do not firmly know ሳእር. It must be a container, since the next clause says ማየ ሳእር 'the water of the ሳእር' runs onto his feet, so I read 'water-skin' with (?). ስንቁ 'his provisions' (ስንቅ + -ሁ, vowel run together). ዓሣእኒሁ 'his sandals' (?): ሣእን is a sandal as I recall it, with the plural and the -ኒሁ suffix; uncertain. ሐቌሁ 'his loins, waist'. ለዕፀውኒ: ለ- (object marker) + ዕፀው 'trees, wood, sticks' + -ኒ 'also'; ደመሮን 'he had gathered them' (ደመረ 'gather, add together' + -ን 'them'). ብሉያት 'worn' (feminine plural of ብሉይ, 'old, worn') and ሥጡጣት 'torn' (from ሠጠጠ 'tear'; both agree with the plural አልባሲሁ 'his clothes'). ሃፉ 'his sweat' (ሃፍ 'sweat' + -ሁ, as I recall; uncertain); ያንጠበጥብ 'it drips' (a quadriliteral stem). ይውኅዝ 'it flows' (ውኅዘ). ሰኰናሁ 'his feet' (ሰኰና, properly 'hoof, sole').

sentences.t: ወኀለፈ ፡ እንተ ፡ ቅድሜሁ ።
sentences.l: And-he-passed [əntä] before-him.
sentences.i: He passed by in front of him.
sentences.n: ወኀለፈ 'and he passed' (ኀለፈ 'pass, go by'; the laborer). ቅድሜሁ 'before him' (ቅድሜ 'front' + -ሁ). I cannot place እንተ here. As a word it is the feminine relative 'which', which cannot be meant. It may be a preposition 'along, past', but I am not sure, so I leave it out of the English.

sentences.t: ወእንዘ ፡ የሐውር ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ ቁም ፡ ወቆመ ፤
sentences.l: And-while he-walks, he-said-to-him: Stand! And-he-stood;
sentences.i: and, as he went, Solomon said to him, "Stop," and he stopped.
sentences.n: ወእንዘ የሐውር 'and while he walks' (ሐወረ 'go, walk'; the laborer). ይቤሎ 'he said to him' (ይቤ 'he said' + ሎ 'to him'; Solomon speaking). ቁም 'stand!' is the imperative of ቆመ; ወቆመ 'and he stood' is the perfect. The pattern ('say X' and 'X was done') shows a royal command obeyed at once.

sentences.t: ወተመይጠ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ ርእዪ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ምንት ፡ ፍድፍድናየ ፡ እምነ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ወምንት ፡ ኅይስናየ ፡ እምነዝ ፡ ወምንት ፡ ክብርየ ፡ እምነ ፡ ከመዝ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-turned to the-queen and-said-to-her: See [fem.] this: what [is] my-superiority(?) than this, and-what my-goodness(?) than this, and-what my-honor than such-a-one?
sentences.i: Then he turned to the queen and said to her, "Look at this man. What is my advantage over him? What is my excellence beyond his? What is my honor compared with one like him?
sentences.n: ወተመይጠ 'and he turned' (ተመይጠ, the ተ- stem of መይጠ 'turn, return'); ኀበ 'to'; ንግሥት 'queen' here stands bare, as a title. ርእዪ is the feminine imperative of ርእየ 'see' (to the queen). ምንት 'what' is followed by three nouns with the suffix -የ 'my': ፍድፍድናየ, ኅይስናየ, ክብርየ. ፍድፍድና is, I think, 'superiority, excess' (cf. ፍድፋድ 'abundance'), and ኅይስና 'goodness, excellence' (?); both are guesses from the sequence, which climbs to ክብር 'honor'. እምነ 'than, beyond' makes the comparison: እምነ ዝንቱ 'than this one', እምነዝ 'than this' (with the demonstrative ዝ), እምነ ከመዝ 'than the like of this'. The three questions are one rhetorical question; a king asks what separates him from a laborer.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አነሂ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወሐመድ ፡ ዘጌሠመ ፡ እከውን ፡ ዕፄ ፡ ወጺአት ፡ ወይእዜ ፡ እንከ ፡ ኣስተርኢ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘኢይመውት ፡ ለዓለም ።
sentences.l: For I-also [am] man and-dust, who tomorrow(?) I-shall-be [ʿəṣe] and-[ṣiʾät(?)]; and-now yet I-appear as one-who not-dies for-ever.
sentences.i: For I too am a man and dust, and tomorrow I shall be [ʿəṣe] and [ṣiʾät] (?); and yet now I appear as one who will never die.
sentences.n: እስመ 'for'; አነሂ 'I also' (አነ + -ኒ/-ሂ, the enclitic 'also, indeed'). ሐመድ 'dust, ashes' recalls Genesis 3:19 and the creation from earth that closes the previous part. ዘጌሠመ: ዘ- + ጌሠም 'tomorrow', literally 'of tomorrow, who tomorrow'; the case-ending is unusual, so uncertain. The words ዕፄ and ወጺአት I cannot read. ዕፄ elsewhere is 'emperor', which cannot be meant here, and ጺአት is unknown to me (a word for corruption or dung would suit, but I do not know it), so both are left in brackets. እከውን 'I shall be' (ኮነ). ወይእዜ እንከ 'and now then, and yet now'. ኣስተርኢ 'I appear, am made to appear' (አስተርአየ, the causative-reflexive of ርእየ 'see'). ዘኢይመውት 'who does not die' (ዘ- + negative ኢ- + ይመውት), ለዓለም 'forever'. The sense is clear: Solomon, in his glory, is as mortal as the laborer.

sentences.t: መኑ ፡ እምአግአዞ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ እመ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ ለዝንቱ ፡ ከማየ ፡ ወሊተኒ ፡ ሶበ ፡ አገበረኒ ፡ ከማሁ ፤
sentences.l: Who from-[he-freed]-him to-God, if he-gave to-this-one like-me, and-to-me also, when he-made-me-work like-him?
sentences.i: Who could have bound God (?), so that he would not give this man what I have, or make me work like him?
sentences.n: This is a hard sentence and my reading is uncertain. መኑ 'who?'; እምአግአዞ 'from he-freed/released him' (እም- + አግአዘ, which usually means 'set free, release' + -ሆ 'him'); ለእግዚኣብሔር 'to/for God'. I take the sense to be 'who could constrain God?', that is, nothing stopped God from making the two of them alike. The rest is plainer: እመ ወሀቦ ለዝንቱ ከማየ 'if he had given to this one like me' (ወሀበ 'give' + -ሁ 'him'; ከማየ 'like me'), ወሊተኒ ሶበ አገበረኒ ከማሁ 'and to me too, when he made me work like him' (ሊተ 'to me' + -ኒ 'also'; አገበረ, the causative of ገብረ, 'make (someone) work', + -ኒ 'me'; ከማሁ 'like him'). The English joins the two halves as 'give this man my lot, or give me his'; that is an interpretation.

sentences.t: አኮኑ ፡ ክልኤነ ፡ ሰንቡእ ፤
sentences.l: Are-we-not two [sänbuʾ]?
sentences.i: Are we two not [sänbuʾ] (?)
sentences.n: አኮኑ 'is it not so?' (አኮ 'not' + -ኑ, the question particle). ክልኤነ 'two (of us)' (ክልኤቱ 'two' with the ending -ነ 'we'). ሰንቡእ I do not know. The next unit glosses it with ሰብእ 'man', so it may be a variant or dialect form of 'man' (or a form from the root of 'human'); I keep the bracket.

sentences.t: ሰብእ ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: [Sänbuʾ] means man.
sentences.i: (that is, "man").
sentences.n: ሰብእ ብሂል 'man, that is to say' (ብሂል is the verbal noun of ይቤ 'say', literally 'a saying/meaning', used as a gloss formula 'that is, meaning'). The sentence defines the preceding word.

sentences.t: ወከመ ፡ ሞተዝ ፡ ሞትየ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ሕይወተዝ ፡ ሕይወትየ ፡ ወዝንቱ ፡ ይጸንዕ ፡ በግብር ፡ እምኔየ ፡ እስመ ፡ ይሁቦሙ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ ለድኩማን ፡ በከመ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ ለሊሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-as this death my-death and-as this life my-life; and-this one is-strong in-work than-me, for he-gives-them strength to-the-weak as he-willed himself;
sentences.i: As this man's death, so is mine; as his life, so is mine. And he is stronger than I in work, for God gives strength to the weak as he himself wills.
sentences.n: ወከመ ሞተዝ ሞትየ 'and as this death (is), my death': ሞት 'death' + the demonstrative -ዝ 'this'; the same in ሕይወተዝ ሕይወትየ 'this life, my life', and in each case the verb 'is' is understood. ወዝንቱ 'and this one'; ይጸንዕ 'he is strong' (ጸንዐ), በግብር 'in work' (ግብር 'work, deed'), እምኔየ 'than me' (እም- + -ኔየ). እስመ 'for'; ይሁቦሙ 'he gives them' (ይሁብ + -ሙ), ኀይለ 'strength' (accusative), ለድኩማን 'to the weak' (ድኩም plural; ለ- marks the recipient). በከመ ፈቀደ ለሊሁ 'as he himself desired' (ፈቀደ 'wish, will'; ለሊሁ 'himself' for emphasis). The subject of ይሁቦሙ is God.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ሖር ፡ ኀበ ፡ ግብርከ ፨
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-him: Go to your-work.
sentences.i: Then he said to him, "Go to your work."
sentences.n: ወይቤሎ 'and he said to him'; ሖር 'go!' (imperative of ሖረ); ኀበ 'to'; ግብርከ 'your work' (ግብር + -ከ). The unit ends with the mark ፨, which in Bezold closes a section (cf. the ten marks at the end of the chapter).

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤላ ፡ ለንግሥት ፡ ምንት ፡ በቊዔትነ ፡ ለእጓለ ፡ እመሕያው ፡ ለእመ ፡ ኢገበርነ ፡ ንስሐ ፡ ወምሕረተ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said-to-her to-the-queen: What [is] our-benefit, to-the-sons-of man, if we-do-not-do repentance and-mercy upon earth?
sentences.i: And again he said to the queen, "What good is it to us, the children of men, if we do not practice repentance and mercy on earth?
sentences.n: ወካዕበ 'and again'; ይቤላ 'he said to her' (ይቤ + ላ). ንግሥት is in apposition to ላ: the pronoun and the noun together, 'to her, to the queen'. ምንት 'what?'; በቊዔትነ 'our benefit' (ቊዔት 'profit, benefit' + -ነ 'our'; በ- here 'in/for', the unit reads 'what is in our benefit'). ለእጓለ እመሕያው 'to the offspring of man' (እጓለ is the construct of እጓል 'offspring, child'; እመሕያው 'of man', literally 'of the mother of the living', is the standard word for 'human being'; so 'son of man', as in the Psalms and the Gospels). ለእመ 'if' (ለ- + እመ); ኢገበርነ 'we did not do' (negative ኢ- + perfect ገበርነ, 'we did'), ንስሐ 'repentance', ምሕረተ 'mercy' (accusative), በዲበ ምድር 'upon the earth'. These two virtues, repentance and mercy, set the sermon's theme.

sentences.t: አኮኑ ፡ ኵልነ ፡ ከንቱ ፡ ሣዕረ ፡ ገዳም ፡ ዘበጊዜሃ ፡ ይየብስ ፡ ወያውዕዮ ፡ እሳት ፤
sentences.l: Are-we-not all vanity, grass-of wilderness which in-its-time withers, and-fire burns-it?
sentences.i: Are we not all vanity, like the grass of the wilderness that withers in its season and that fire burns?
sentences.n: አኮኑ 'is it not so?'; ኵልነ 'all of us' (ኵሉ + -ነ); ከንቱ 'vain, empty' (cf. Ecclesiastes 1:2). ሣዕረ ገዳም is a construct, 'grass of the wilderness' (ሣዕር 'grass', ገዳም 'wilderness'), standing in apposition. ዘበጊዜሃ ይየብስ 'which in its time withers' (ዘ- 'which' + በ- 'in' + ጊዜ 'time' + -ሃ 'its'; ይየብስ, የብሰ 'be dry'). ወያውዕዮ 'and it burns it' (አውዐየ 'burn', causative; the subject አሳት 'fire' follows). The image echoes Isaiah 40:6-8 and Psalm 103 (102):15-16, where human life is grass; cf. Psalm 37 (36):2.

sentences.t: በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ንትረሰይ ፡ በመባልዕት ፡ ጥዑማት ፡ ወበአልባስ ፡ ክቡራት ፤
sentences.l: Upon earth we-are-made(?) with-foods sweet and-with-clothing precious;
sentences.i: On earth we make ourselves comfortable (?) with sweet food and costly clothing,
sentences.n: ንትረሰይ 'we are made / we make ourselves': ተረሰየ is the passive-reflexive of ረሰየ 'make, set'. The English 'make ourselves comfortable' is an interpretation. በመባልዕት ጥዑማት 'with foods, sweet ones' (መብልዕ 'food', plural መባልዕት; ጥዑም 'sweet'; the adjective agrees as plural feminine), ወበአልባስ ክቡራት 'and with clothing, precious ones'. The two parallel constructions (እንዘ 'while' + noun + adjective) in the following lines contrast outward ease with inward ruin.

sentences.t: እንዘ ፡ ሕያዋን ፡ ጽዩኣን ፤
sentences.l: while living, loathsome(?);
sentences.i: though we are alive, we are loathsome (?);
sentences.n: እንዘ ሕያዋን ጽዩኣን 'while living ones, [ṣəyuʾan]'. ሕያዋን is the plural of ሕያው 'living'. ጽዩኣን is the plural of ጽዩእ; I am not sure of it. It may come from ጸየአ 'be foul, loathsome', which would suit the contrast with ሕያዋን. The series that follows ('alive, but dead; wise, but fools; honored, but lacking') makes a negative sense very likely.

sentences.t: ወንትረሰይ ፡ በመዐዛት ፡ ወበዕፍረታት ፤
sentences.l: and-we-make-ourselves with-fragrances and-with-ointments(?);
sentences.i: we make ourselves fragrant with perfumes and ointments,
sentences.n: ወንትረሰይ is the same verb as above, 'we make ourselves' (so I render it 'make ourselves fragrant'). መዐዛት 'fragrances' (plural of መዐዛ 'sweet smell'), ዕፍረታት 'ointments, perfumes' (plural of ዕፍረት). በ- 'with'.

sentences.t: እንዘ ፡ ሕያዋን ፡ ምዉታን ፡ በኀጢዓት ፡ ወበዓበሳት ፤
sentences.l: while living, dead in-sins and-in-offences(?);
sentences.i: though we are alive, we are dead in sins and in offences (?);
sentences.n: ምዉታን 'dead ones' (plural of ምዉት). ኀጢዓት 'sin' (plural, or the collective form, 'sins'); ዓበሳት 'offences, transgressions' (?), from ዓበስ, which I do not know well. 'Dead in sins' recalls Ephesians 2:1.

sentences.t: እንዘ ፡ ጠቢባን ፡ ኮነ ፡ አብዳነ ፡ በኢሰሚዕ ፡ ወበዕልወታት ፤
sentences.l: while wise, we-became fools through-not-hearing and-through-perversities(?);
sentences.i: though we are wise, we have become fools through not listening and through perversities (?);
sentences.n: ጠቢባን 'wise ones' (plural of ጠቢብ), ኮነ 'we became' (the form ኮነ is 3ms; a plural 'we became' would be ኮንነ, so Bezold's form is odd, perhaps a mistake for ኮነ read as a general 'it came to be'). አብዳነ 'fools' (accusative plural of አብድ, 'foolish'). በኢሰሚዕ 'through not-hearing' (negative ኢ- + the noun ሰሚዕ; the infinitive-like 'disobedience'). ዕልወታት 'perversities' (?): possibly from ዐልወ 'be crooked, perverse'; uncertain. The echo is Romans 1:22, 'claiming to be wise they became fools'.

sentences.t: እንዘ ፡ ክቡራን ፡ ኮነ ፡ ኅሱራነ ፡ በተጠይሮ ፡ ወበሰጊድ ፡ ለጣዖት ።
sentences.l: while honored, we-became lacking through-[täṭäyro] and-through-bowing to-idols.
sentences.i: though we are honored, we have become lacking through [täṭäyro] (?) and through bowing down to idols.
sentences.n: ክቡራን 'honored ones' (plural of ክቡር); ኅሱራነ 'deficient, lacking' (accusative plural of ኅሱር 'wanting'); the same as in the previous unit, ኮነ is used for 'we became'. ተጠይሮ I cannot identify. Since it is joined with idol-worship it may name a pagan practice, perhaps augury, but that is a guess; I leave it as [täṭäyro]. ሰጊድ 'bowing, worship' (the verbal noun of ሰገደ), ጣዖት 'idols' (Greek loan; ለ- 'to'). The rhetoric (ምዉታን, አብዳን, ኅሱራን) is that of the preacher against the Queen's idol-worshiping people: Solomon is shaping his argument toward her question.

sentences.t: ሰብእሰ ፡ ክቡር ፡ ዘተፈጥረ ፡ በአምሳለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወለእመኒ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ይከውን ፡ ከመ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: Man indeed [is] honorable who-was-created in-the-likeness-of God, and-if he-does good he-becomes like God;
sentences.i: Man is honorable, for he was created in the likeness of God, and if he does good he becomes like God.
sentences.n: ሰብእሰ 'man indeed, but man' (ሰብእ + the contrastive enclitic -ሰ; it sets 'man as made' against 'man as acting'). ክቡር 'honored'. ዘተፈጥረ 'who was created' (ተፈጥረ, the passive of ፈጠረ 'create'). በአምሳለ እግዚኣብሔር 'in the likeness of God': አምሳለ is the construct of አምሳል, 'likeness, image', followed by the name; so 'in God's image'. The allusion is to Genesis 1:26-27, and the previous part ended on the same thought. ወለእመኒ ገብረ ሠናየ 'and if he did good' (ለእመ 'if' + -ኒ, ገብረ 'did', ሠናየ 'good', accusative); ይከውን 'he becomes' (ኮነ, imperfect), ከመ 'like'.

sentences.t: ሰብእሰ ፡ ከንቱ ፡ ወለእመኒ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ኀጢአተ ፡ ይከውን ፡ ከመ ፡ ዲያብሎስ ፤
sentences.l: Man indeed [is] vain, and-if he-does sin he-becomes like the-Devil;
sentences.i: But man is vain, and if he commits sin he becomes like the Devil.
sentences.n: The mirror of the previous unit. ከንቱ 'vain, worthless'. ኀጢአተ 'sin' (accusative). ዲያብሎስ is the Greek διάβολος 'slanderer, devil'.

sentences.t: ዲያብሎስሰ ፡ ዕቡይ ፡ ዘዓበየ ፡ ተአዝዞ ፡ ለፈጣሪሁ ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ ዕቡያን ፡ እምሰብእ ፡ የሐውሩ ፡ በፍኖቱ ፡ ወይትኴነኑ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፤
sentences.l: The-Devil indeed [is] proud, who grew-great(?) in-obeying to-his-Creator; and-all the-proud from-men walk in-his-way, and-are-condemned with-him;
sentences.i: The Devil is proud, for he refused to obey his Creator. And all the proud among men walk in his way and are condemned along with him.
sentences.n: ዲያብሎስሰ 'the Devil indeed' (-ሰ contrastive again). ዕቡይ 'proud'. ዘዓበየ ተአዝዞ ለፈጣሪሁ: ዓበየ 'was great, was arrogant' (ዓበየ also 'become great'); ተአዝዞ is the verbal noun of ተአዘዘ 'obey' (so 'in/regarding obeying'); ለፈጣሪሁ 'to his Creator' (ፈጣሪ, the agent noun of ፈጠረ 'create', + -ሁ). I take ዓበየ in its bad sense, 'was insolent', which yields 'refused to obey'; that is an interpretation. ኵሎሙ ዕቡያን 'all the proud'. እምሰብእ 'from among men'. የሐውሩ 'they walk', በፍኖቱ 'in his way' (ፍኖት 'road, way'; 'to walk in the way' is a biblical image for conduct, as in Psalm 1). ይትኴነኑ 'they are condemned, judged' (ተኴነነ, passive of ኴነነ 'judge'); ምስሌሁ 'with him'.

sentences.t: ወእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ያፈቅሮሙ ፡ ለትሑታን ፡ ወእለ ፡ ይገብሩ ፡ ትሕትና ፡ የሐውሩ ፡ በፍኖቱ ፡ ወይትፌሥሑ ፡ በውስተ ፡ መንግሥቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-God loves-them the-humble, and-those who practice humility walk in-his-way and-rejoice in-his-kingdom;
sentences.i: But God loves the humble, and those who practice humility walk in his way and rejoice in his kingdom.
sentences.n: ወእግዚኣብሔር 'and God' (here 'but'). ያፈቅሮሙ ለትሑታን 'he loves them, the humble' (አፍቀረ 'love'; the pronoun ሙ 'them' is repeated by the noun with ለ-; a regular Geʿez pattern of anticipating the object). ወእለ ይገብሩ ትሕትና 'and those who do humility' (እለ 'those who', ትሕትና 'humility', from ትሑት 'humble'). ይትፌሥሑ 'they rejoice' (ተፈሥሐ); መንግሥቱ 'his kingdom'. Compare Psalm 25 (24):9 and Matthew 5:3-5, where the humble inherit.

sentences.t: ወብፁዕሰ ፡ ዘአእመረ ፡ ጥበበ ፡ ዝውእቱ ፡ ንስሐ ፡ ወፈሪሀ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፨
sentences.l: And-blessed [is] he-who-knew wisdom, that-is repentance and-the-fear-of God.
sentences.i: Blessed is he who has known wisdom, which is repentance and the fear of God."
sentences.n: ወብፁዕሰ 'and blessed indeed' (ብፁዕ 'blessed', the -ሰ contrastive). ዘአእመረ 'who knew' (አእመረ 'know'); ጥበበ 'wisdom' (accusative); ዝውእቱ 'that is' (literally 'this is' ዝ + ውእቱ). ፈሪሀ is the construct of ፈሪሆት/ፈሪህ 'fear', here followed by እግዚኣብሔር 'of God'. The thought is that of Proverbs 1:7 and 9:10, 'the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom', and Psalm 111 (110):10. Solomon's speech ends here, with ፨.

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ ሰሚዓ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ትቤ ፡ ምንተ ፡ ሠነየኒ ፡ ቃልከ ፡ ወእፎ ፡ ሐወዘኒ ፡ ነገርከ ፡ ወመክሥተ ፡ አፉከ ።
sentences.l: And-this having-heard, the-queen she-said: How-pleasing-to-me your-word, and-how-sweet-to-me your-speech, and-the-opening-of your-mouth.
sentences.i: When the queen heard this, she said, "How pleasing to me are your words, how sweet your speech, and the opening of your mouth!
sentences.n: ሰሚዓ 'having heard' (the gerund of ሰምዐ), the same type as ርእዮ above. ንግሥት 'the queen' follows as subject. ትቤ 'she said' (the feminine of ይቤ). ምንተ 'how, what' used as an exclamation. ሠነየኒ 'it pleased me' (ሠነየ 'be good, pleasing' + -ኒ 'me'); ሐወዘኒ 'it was sweet to me' (ሐወዘ 'be sweet' + -ኒ). እፎ 'how'. ቃልከ 'your word' (ቃል + -ከ); ነገርከ 'your speech'; ወመክሥተ አፉከ 'and the opening of your mouth': መክሥት 'opening' is a construct with አፉከ 'your mouth' (አፍ 'mouth' with the old -ው-/-ኡ- stem before a suffix); it is accusative -ä, loose syntax, as an added exclamation.

sentences.t: ንግረኒኬ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ይረትዕ ፡ ለዘ ፡ እሰግድ ፡ ሎቱ ፤
sentences.l: Tell-me then of-the-one who is-true, to-whom I-bow to-him;
sentences.i: Now tell me who is the true one, the one to whom I should bow down.
sentences.n: ንግረኒኬ 'tell me, then' (ንግር, imperative of ነገረ 'tell', + -ኒ 'me' + -ኬ, an enclitic 'then, now'). ለዘ ይረትዕ 'of the one who is true' (ዘ- 'who' + ይረትዕ, from ረትዐ 'be true, straight, right'); ለዘ እሰግድ ሎቱ 'to whom I bow to him' (the relative pronoun is repeated by ሎቱ 'to him', as normal in Geʿez; ሰገደ 'bow, worship'). The queen asks whom she should serve, the central question of the whole book.

sentences.t: ወንሕነሰ ፡ ንሰግድ ፡ ለፀሐይ ፡ በከመ ፡ መሀሩነ ፡ አበዊነ ፡ እስመ ፡ ንብል ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ ንጉሦሙ ፡ ለአማልክት ፤
sentences.l: And-we-indeed we-bow to-the-sun as taught-us our-fathers, for we-say: he [is] the-sun, king-of the-gods;
sentences.i: As for us, we bow down to the sun, as our fathers taught us, because we say that the sun is king of the gods;
sentences.n: ወንሕነሰ 'and we indeed' (-ሰ contrasts 'we' with 'others', which comes next). ንሰግድ 'we bow' (ሰገደ 'bow'); ለፀሐይ 'to the sun'; በከመ 'as, according as'; መሀሩነ 'they taught us' (መሀረ 'teach' + -ነ); አበዊነ 'our fathers'. እስመ ንብል 'because we say'; ውእቱ ፀሐይ 'he is the sun'; ንጉሦሙ ለአማልክት 'their king, (that of) the gods': ንጉሥ with the suffix ሙ 'their' and the following ለ- noun is a regular construction for 'the king of the gods'. አማልክት, plural of አምላክ 'god'.

sentences.t: ወባዕዳንሂ ፡ እለ ፡ እምታሕቴነ ፡ ቦእለ ፡ ይሰግዱ ፡ ለዓእባን ፡ ወቦ ፡ እለ ፡ ይሰግዱ ፡ ለአዕዋም ፡ ወቦእለ ፡ ይሰግዱ ፡ ለግልፈዋት ፡ ወቦ ፡ እለ ፡ ይሰግዱ ፡ ለአምሳለ ፡ ወርቅ ፡ ወብሩር ፤
sentences.l: And-others, those who [are] beneath-us, there-are-those-who they-bow to-stones, and-there-are those who they-bow to-trees, and-there-are-those who they-bow to-[gəlfäwat], and-there-are those who they-bow to-the-likeness-of gold and-silver;
sentences.i: And others, those below us, include some who bow down to stones, some who bow to trees, some who bow to carved things (?), and some who bow to images of gold and silver.
sentences.n: ወባዕዳንሂ 'and others too' (ባዕድ 'other, foreign', plural ባዕዳን; -ሂ 'too'). እለ እምታሕቴነ 'those who are beneath us' (እም-ታሕተ 'from beneath' + -ነ; the Queen's subjects). ቦእለ / ወቦ እለ 'there are those who' (ቦ 'there is' + እለ 'those who'); ይሰግዱ 'they bow'. ዓእባን 'stones' (plural of እብን); አዕዋም 'trees' (?): I am not sure of the word (it might also be 'pillars'), but 'trees' fits the list. ግልፈዋት is probably the plural of ግልፈት 'carved thing' (from ገለፈ 'carve, engrave'); (?). አምሳለ ወርቅ ወብሩር 'the likeness of gold and silver': አምሳለ is a construct, so 'images made of gold and silver' (compare Psalm 115 (113):4, 'idols of silver and gold').

sentences.t: ወንሕነሰ ፡ ንሰግድ ፡ ለፀሐይ ፡ እስመ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ያበስል ፡ ሲሳየ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ያበርህ ፡ ጽልመተ ፡ ወያአትት ፡ ፍርሀተ ፤
sentences.l: And-we-indeed we-bow to-the-sun, for he cooks(?) food, and-again he makes-bright darkness and-removes fear;
sentences.i: We bow to the sun because he ripens (?) our food, and because he makes the darkness light and takes away fear.
sentences.n: ያበስል 'he cooks, ripens' (አብሰለ, the causative of በሰለ 'be ripe, cooked'); ሲሳየ 'food, sustenance' (accusative); ወካዕበ 'and again, and moreover'; ያበርህ 'he makes bright' (አብርሀ, the causative of በርሀ 'be bright'); ጽልመተ 'darkness' (accusative); ያአትት 'he removes, takes away' (አአተተ; the stem I know less well); ፍርሀተ 'fear' (accusative). The three benefits are the queen's reasons for sun-worship: food, light, and security from night.

sentences.t: ንብሎ ፡ ንጉሥነ ፡ ወንብሎ ፡ ፈጣሪነ ፡ ወንሰግድ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ከመ ፡ አምላክነ ፤
sentences.l: We-call-him our-king, and-we-call-him our-creator, and-we-bow to-him as our-God;
sentences.i: We call him our king and our creator, and we bow down to him as our God,
sentences.n: ንብሎ 'we say to him, we call him' (ይቤ + ሎ), repeated for emphasis; ንጉሥነ 'our king', ፈጣሪነ 'our creator' (the word used for God in Solomon's speech, ፈጣሪሁ above); ንሰግድ ሎቱ 'we bow to him'; ከመ አምላክነ 'as our god'. The word ፈጣሪ is repeated on purpose: the queen applies to the sun the very title Solomon gave to God.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘነገረነ ፡ ባዕደ ፡ ዓምላከ ፡ ዘእንበሌሁ ።
sentences.l: for there-is-not who-told-us another god besides-him.
sentences.i: for no one has told us of any other god besides him.
sentences.n: እስመ አልቦ 'for there is not'; ዘነገረነ 'who told us' (ነገረ + -ነ); ባዕደ ዓምላከ 'another god' (accusative: ባዕድ 'other' and አምላክ, the initial vowel being written ዓ-); ዘእንበሌሁ 'besides him, without him' (ዘእንበለ + -ሁ). The sentence closes her statement of belief with ።.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ሰማዕነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ብክሙአ ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ ካልአ ፡ አምላከ ፡ ዘኢናአምሮ ፡ ንሕነ ፡ ወዜነዉነ ፡ ከመ ፡ አውረደ ፡ ለክሙ ፡ ታቦተ ፡ እምሰማያት ፡ ወወሀበክሙ ፡ ጽላተ ፡ ሥርዐተ ፡ መላእክት ፡ በእደ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ነቢዩ ፡ ሰማዕነ ፡ ዘንተ ፤
sentences.l: But we-heard that you-have, Israel, another god whom not we-know, we; and-they-told-us that he-brought-down for-you the-Ark from-the-heavens, and-he-gave-you tablets, the-ordinance-of angels, by-the-hand-of Moses the-prophet; we-heard this;
sentences.i: But we have heard that you, Israel, have another God whom we do not know. They told us that he brought down the Ark for you from the heavens, and gave you the tablets, the ordinance of the angels, by the hand of Moses the prophet. This we have heard;
sentences.n: ወባሕቱ 'but'. ሰማዕነ 'we heard' (ሰምዐ). ብክሙአ 'you (pl.) have' (ብ- 'there is to' + ክሙ 'you'), with an extra -አ that I cannot explain (an interrogative particle, perhaps, but she is reporting what she has heard, so I do not render it). ለእስራኤል 'to Israel': the vocative or apposition. ካልአ አምላከ 'another god' (accusative). ዘኢናአምሮ ንሕነ 'whom we do not know' (ዘ- + ኢ- + ናአምሮ, from አእመረ 'know', + the pronoun ሮ 'him'; ንሕነ 'we' repeats the subject for stress). ወዜነዉነ 'and they told us' (ዜነወ 'tell, report'). ከመ አውረደ 'that he brought down' (አውረደ, the causative of ወረደ 'descend'). ለክሙ 'for you'. ታቦተ 'the Ark' (accusative of ታቦት): the Ark is central to the book. The queen already speaks of it as something that came down from heaven, which is the book's own view, not Exodus 25. ወወሀበክሙ 'and he gave you'. ጽላተ 'tablets' (accusative), ሥርዐተ መላእክት 'the ordinance of the angels': ሥርዐተ is a construct, 'ordinance of'. The reference to angels is that of the later tradition that the Law came 'through angels' (Acts 7:53; Galatians 3:19; Hebrews 2:2). በእደ ሙሴ ነቢዩ 'by the hand of Moses his prophet' (ነቢይ 'prophet' + -ሁ, which makes 'Moses, the prophet'; I take the suffix as the definite sense). ሰማዕነ ዘንተ 'we heard this' repeats the opening verb to close the report.

sentences.t: ወይወርድ ፡ አ ፡ ኀቤክሙ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ወይትናገረክሙ ፡ ወይኤምረክሙ ፡ ፍትሖ ፡ ወትእዛዞ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-does-he-come-down [ʾa] to-you himself, and-speak-with-you, and-teach-you his-judgment and-his-commandment?
sentences.i: Does he himself come down to you, and speak with you, and teach you his judgment and his commandments?"
sentences.n: ወይወርድ አ ኀቤክሙ ለሊሁ: ይወርድ 'he comes down' (ወረደ). I take the detached አ as the question particle (written apart from the verb here), so 'does he come down...?' If that is wrong the sentence is a plain statement, 'and he comes down to you himself'. ኀቤክሙ 'to you' (ኀበ + -ክሙ); ለሊሁ 'himself'. ይትናገረክሙ 'he speaks with you' (ተናገረ + -ክሙ); ይኤምረክሙ 'he teaches you, makes you know' (አምረ, the causative of አእመረ 'know'; the 3ms is spelled ይኤምር). ፍትሖ 'his judgment' (ፍትሕ + -ሁ, vowel written -ሖ), ትእዛዞ 'his commandment' (ትእዛዝ + -ሁ). The chapter ends with a run of ten ፨ marks, which are a section close; they stay on the last unit. Her speech turns, as it will for several chapters, to Israel's God.
